sentences.text:
Subsequently, the charge sheet has been filed under Sections 376, 377,
379, 384, 323, 328, 506, 509 of IPC.
The application seeking regular bail having been rejected by the High Court vide impugned order dated 30.04.2025, the appellant has preferred the instant appeal.
Mr.Shikhar Srivastava, learned counsel submitted that initially he was instructed to appear for the second respondent-complainant.
However, he does not have any vakalatnama or further instructions in the matter.
His submission is placed on record.
In the circumstances, we have heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Additional Solicitor General for the first respondent-State.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that after a detailed hearing, this Court granted interim bail vide order dated 28.05.2025 pending appearance of the second respondent-complainant.
There is no appearance on behalf of the second respondent- complainant which is due to obvious reasons.

sentences.text: He submitted that the second respondent-complainant is about forty-two years of age, whereas the appellant is half her age being only twenty one years; the allegations as against the appellant herein are wholly frivolous; that possibly there were certain business transactions between the two which may have gone sour.
Further, the relationship between the parties being consensual in nature, there cannot be any criminal allegations as such against the appellant herein.
He further submitted that the charges have not yet been framed, but the appellant was in jail since 07.08.2024 till he was released on interim bail on 28.05.2025.

Having regard to the totality of the facts and circumstances of this case and the allegations against the appellant herein being frivolous and false, the appeal may be allowed by granting regular bail to the appellant herein.
Per contra, learned Additional Solicitor General appearing for the first respondent submitted that the fact as to whether there was a consensual relationship or not is debatable.
However, the appellant indulged in blackmailing the second respondent-complainant.
In the circumstances, the complainant was constrained to file the criminal complaint as against the appellant.
There is no merit in the appeal and hence, the same may be dismissed.
Considering the facts on record, in our view, the appellant is entitled for regular bail.

Consequently,
we set aside the impugned order.
At this stage, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant has to appear before the concerned Sessions Court on 19.09.2025.

We, therefore, allow this appeal and direct as under:
The appellant shall appear before the concerned Sessions Court on 19.09.2025, who shall release him on regular bail subject to the terms and conditions to be imposed on the appellant herein.
With these observations, the appeal is allowed.
NEW DELHI SEPTEMBER 4, 2025.
